transcripts.name: 01 Exports
transcripts.text:
# Harbor Desk discovery 01 — Reporting handoff

Mira (analyst): Before we start, did the projector arrive back from the library? The rain was impressive this morning.
Nora (cooperative lead): It did, and the case was dry. Let us start with reports before we forget why we booked this call.
Mira (analyst): The approved document lets coordinators view reports and only administrators export them. Is the complaint about the report itself or the access rule?
Nora (cooperative lead): Both, but they are separate. Coordinators must be allowed to export reservation reports too.
Mira (analyst): That changes the administrator-only export policy. I will mark it as a conflict, not assume the change is approved. Do you still need CSV?
Nora (cooperative lead): Keep the export as UTF-8 CSV using the active filters.
Owen (coordinator): I first thought PDF because people print things, but no, forget PDF for this release. CSV is what we actually send to our internal spreadsheet.
Mira (analyst): Good, I will not turn the withdrawn PDF idea into a requirement. What is missing from the current manual process?
Owen (coordinator): At month end I keep adding up reservations by hand. Add a monthly reservation count to the report.
Mira (analyst): Do you mean one total for the selected interval, or a month-by-month breakdown? The report already has filter-matched counts above the rows.
Owen (coordinator): A month-by-month breakdown, even if the date filter spans three months. The ordinary total can stay where it is.
Nora (cooperative lead): Yes. Add a month-by-month reservation count to the report, grouped by reservation start month.
Mira (analyst): Is scheduled email needed now?
Nora (cooperative lead): Not now. We can download manually; please do not invent a scheduler because I said month end.
Owen (coordinator): One other thing: make exporting feel instant.
Mira (analyst): That needs a report size and a time target. We have not agreed either. I will leave a question rather than a performance acceptance criterion.
Nora (cooperative lead): Fine. I need to take the next call, so send the access-policy question separately. The board has not approved broader exports yet.

transcripts.name: 02 Retention
transcripts.text:
# Harbor Desk discovery 02 — Audit review

Mira (analyst): Your microphone is much clearer today. Are we still reviewing audit history rather than reservation history?
Eli (administrator): Exactly. The reservations themselves are not what I want to delete. I am talking about the log of who changed things.
Mira (analyst): The baseline keeps audit events for one hundred eighty days and removes older events daily.
Eli (administrator): Keep audit events for three hundred sixty-five days instead of one hundred eighty days.
Mira (analyst): That is a change to the retention policy. Is a reason or approval recorded yet?
Eli (administrator): Not yet. I need the committee to approve it. Our annual review is the reason, but do not tell the developers it is already signed off.
Nora (cooperative lead): I was about to say keep them forever, but that is too broad. Withdraw forever. The proposed change is one year, subject to that review.
Mira (analyst): Understood. What should remain unchanged?
Eli (administrator): Audit events must remain append-only; corrections should create a new event.
Mira (analyst): That matches the specification. How do you find the entry you need?
Eli (administrator): Today I have to open a record first. Allow administrators to filter audit history by actor identifier.
Mira (analyst): We can describe an exact actor filter. Do you also need free-text search?
Eli (administrator): No, not in this change. I said search earlier in the week, but I only need the actor identifier filter. One value at a time is enough.
Nora (cooperative lead): Can you get it to us soon?
Mira (analyst): Soon is not a delivery date. Do you have a deadline linked to the review?
Nora (cooperative lead): I do not have the committee date yet. Put that on the question list; please do not manufacture a date from the annual-review wording.
Eli (administrator): Also, none of this should put invitation tokens into the audit log. I know that is already prohibited. I just wanted to make sure the new filter does not change the recorded data.
Mira (analyst): We will keep the policy change, the new filter and the scheduling question separate. Thanks, and I hope the microphone survives the rest of the afternoon.

transcripts.name: 03 Sharing
transcripts.text:
# Harbor Desk discovery 03 — Invitations and private links

Mira (analyst): Thanks for joining. I can hear the equipment-room door; are you doing handover at the same time?
Owen (coordinator): Only returning a cable, sorry. My problem is that members forward reservation links to somebody collecting equipment for them.
Mira (analyst): A copied URL currently requires sign-in and the normal permission check. What change are you proposing?
Owen (coordinator): Let anyone with a reservation sharing link view that reservation without signing in.
Mira (analyst): That conflicts with the private-access rule. The document explicitly excludes public sharing links. I will raise it as a policy question.
Nora (cooperative lead): Yes, it is a proposal. Perhaps we should just add a named collector instead, but I am not deciding that today. Keep the public-link request visible so the committee sees the privacy tradeoff.
Mira (analyst): We will not silently implement the alternative either. Are the invitation permissions changing?
Owen (coordinator): Coordinators must still be able to invite prospective members by email.
Mira (analyst): That is already in the baseline. What happened with the mistaken invitation last week?
Owen (coordinator): We waited for expiry. Allow a coordinator to revoke an invitation before it expires.
Mira (analyst): What should accepting a revoked invitation do?
Owen (coordinator): Reject it and explain that it was revoked. It must not create an account.
Nora (cooperative lead): I originally asked for reminders as well, but leave reminders out. Revocation is the concrete gap; seventy-two-hour expiry stays.
Mira (analyst): Who else needs access? You mentioned external collaborators in an email.
Nora (cooperative lead): External collaborators should get the right access.
Mira (analyst): We do not have that role or a permission matrix. Which pages and actions, and is it an existing member account?
Nora (cooperative lead): I need to ask the team. Do not guess a role or grant all coordinator permissions.
Owen (coordinator): That sounds sensible. I have to run downstairs now. Please keep revocation separate from the anonymous-link proposal; revocation is useful even if the board rejects public links.

transcripts.name: 04 Bookings
transcripts.text:
# Harbor Desk discovery 04 — Reservation window

Mira (analyst): Shall we use the camera example? We can skip the weather this time, although I see another umbrella by your desk.
Jun (member representative): It is drying. Yes, the camera booking is why I am here. Members plan workshops earlier than the portal lets them reserve.
Mira (analyst): The baseline advance window is fourteen calendar days for every role, and the maximum duration is three days.
Jun (member representative): Allow reservations to start up to thirty calendar days after submission.
Mira (analyst): That conflicts with the fourteen-day limit. Are you proposing a new duration too?
Jun (member representative): No. Keep the maximum duration at three consecutive calendar days.
Nora (cooperative lead): The thirty-day idea needs approval because it changes how early people can claim equipment. Do not hide it as a configuration tweak.
Mira (analyst): What happens if the requested slot is already taken?
Jun (member representative): Let members subscribe to an email when a selected item and date interval become available.
Mira (analyst): A waiting-list style notification is new. Is this automatic reservation when the slot opens?
Jun (member representative): Definitely not. Send an email with a portal link. The member must still submit a reservation, and another person may get there first.
Nora (cooperative lead): I first said book every Thursday, but recurring reservations can wait. Do not create a recurring-booking story from that aside.
Mira (analyst): Should subscriptions have an expiry or an unsubscribe action?
Jun (member representative): Yes, members must be able to unsubscribe. I do not know the expiry rule; please ask us before settling it.
Mira (analyst): We can capture the feature and leave the expiry decision open. Any need for SMS?
Jun (member representative): No, email only. I want the same familiar channel, not another notification system.
Nora (cooperative lead): Good. The practical test for me is cancelling a reservation, getting the email as a subscriber and still having to book manually. We will review the thirty-day rule as a separate policy change.

transcripts.name: 05 Usability
transcripts.text:
# Harbor Desk discovery 05 — Everyday use

Mira (analyst): Did you find the spare keyboard? Last time we were discussing navigation without a mouse.
Jun (member representative): Yes, and I tried a few ordinary websites with it. All core reservation actions must work with a keyboard and visible focus.
Mira (analyst): That repeats the accessibility baseline, which is useful to confirm. We should test it rather than treat it as extra scope.
Owen (coordinator): My repeated task is filtering the catalogue to projectors. Let each member save one personal catalogue filter preset between visits.
Mira (analyst): The baseline has category and date filters, but no saved presets. What belongs in the preset?
Owen (coordinator): Category only. I first thought dates too, but yesterday's dates are not useful next week. Save the category, not the selected dates.
Mira (analyst): Does it replace the default alphabetical ordering?
Owen (coordinator): No. Load the saved category when I return, keep alphabetical ordering, and let me clear the preset. One preset is plenty.
Jun (member representative): The reservation form should be faster.
Mira (analyst): Faster to load, fewer actions to submit, or a shorter server response? How would we measure success?
Jun (member representative): I cannot say yet. We should watch a member do it. Do not invent a two-second target just because I used the word faster.
Mira (analyst): Agreed. Any visual changes needed for status?
Jun (member representative): Keep a text label next to any status color. I know we agreed that before; I am repeating it because the printout lost the colors.
Owen (coordinator): And do not build a whole design system for the saved preset. A clear save and clear control is enough.
Mira (analyst): We will keep the new persistent category choice separate from baseline accessibility and the unresolved usability target. Next time we can look at one observed workflow instead of trying to fix every annoyance at once.

transcripts.name: 06 Operations
transcripts.text:
# Harbor Desk discovery 06 — Support handoff

Mira (analyst): This is our last review before the draft. How did the weekend equipment fair go?
Eli (administrator): Quietly, fortunately. It reminded us that volunteers need to know whether the portal is unavailable without asking an administrator.
Mira (analyst): We currently have an internal health endpoint but no public status page.
Eli (administrator): Add a public read-only status page that shows whether the reservation service is available.
Mira (analyst): Should that page expose bookings or member names?
Eli (administrator): No. Show service availability only, without reservation data, member details or an action to change anything. I initially asked for recent error details, but leave those private.
Nora (cooperative lead): That page is different from a public reservation link. We still need the private-access decision from the earlier call.
Mira (analyst): Yes, the baseline allows a generic anonymous page, so a service-only status page is a new feature, not a change to reservation permissions. What retry behavior should email use?
Eli (administrator): Retry outbound email on 429 or 5xx at most three times after the initial attempt, with exponential backoff.
Mira (analyst): That matches the approved behavior. Any operational constraints we should add?
Nora (cooperative lead): Do not schedule database schema migrations on Saturdays or Sundays.
Mira (analyst): That is new; the baseline has no maintenance schedule. Which timezone should determine the day?
Nora (cooperative lead): Use the cooperative's configured local timezone. Emergency work needs its own decision; do not silently add an emergency bypass here.
Eli (administrator): We should monitor everything too.
Mira (analyst): Which events, thresholds, and who receives alerts? A status page does not define those choices.
Eli (administrator): I do not have that list. Capture the question rather than deploying an alert for every log line.
Mira (analyst): Good. I will return a draft with traceable requirements, not create tasks automatically. You can edit the story and acceptance criteria before approving anything.

Lena (salon owner): Let's skip loyalty for now, maybe next year.

REQ-001.text:
## HD-EXPORT — Report export permissions and format

Only administrators may export reservation reports. Coordinators may view reports but may not download them. The server must enforce this restriction even when a coordinator sends an export request directly. Hiding the export button alone is insufficient. Members have no report export permission. Introducing another role with export permission is a change to the approved access policy, not a clarification of the existing behavior.

The initial export format is CSV encoded as UTF-8. Exported rows follow the active report filters and contain the same approved columns as the report. CSV values that could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas must be rendered safely. The filename includes the export date and does not contain a member's name. PDF, spreadsheet workbooks, scheduled delivery and a new monthly summary column are outside the baseline. Large reports may take time to prepare, but no asynchronous export queue is specified for the first release.
REQ-001.heading: HD-EXPORT — Report export permissions and format

REQ-001.text:
## HD-REPORTS — Reservation reporting

Coordinators and administrators can view a reservation report filtered by date interval, item and reservation status. Each row contains the reservation reference, item name, requested dates and status. Member names are visible only to staff with reporting access. Members can view their own reservation list but not the organization-wide report. Empty reports show a clear empty state rather than an error.

The report is generated on demand from current records. The baseline does not schedule reports, email attachments or save personal report views. Counts shown above the report must use the same filters as the displayed rows. Changing a filter and then exporting must not silently export an older filter selection. The interface should make the active filters visible so a staff member can explain what a report represents.
REQ-001.heading: HD-REPORTS — Reservation reporting

REQ-001.text:
## HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention

Role changes, reservation creation, cancellation and handover confirmation create audit events. Each event records an actor identifier, action, affected record identifier and timestamp. Audit records are append-only: ordinary users, coordinators and administrators cannot edit earlier events through the portal. Corrections are represented by a new event referencing the affected action. Passwords, invitation tokens and session tokens must never be recorded in audit data.

Audit events are retained for one hundred eighty days. A daily cleanup removes events older than that retention period. Administrators can view audit history for a particular affected record, but the baseline does not include a general actor filter or a free-text search across all events. Retaining audit data for a longer period changes the approved retention policy and requires explicit approval. Exporting report rows must not accidentally include audit payloads or account credentials.

The retention rule concerns audit events rather than active reservations. Removing an old audit event does not delete a current booking. Before changing retention, stakeholders must identify both the purpose of longer storage and the records it covers. A vague request to keep everything must not be interpreted as permission for indefinite retention.
REQ-001.heading: HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention

REQ-001.text:
## HD-CATALOGUE — Equipment information

The catalogue contains an item name, category, plain-language description, storage location and availability calendar. Categories are camera, projector and audio kit. An administrator can mark an item out of service with an explanation. An out-of-service item remains visible with its status, but cannot receive new reservations. Existing affected reservations are flagged for coordinator attention rather than silently cancelled.

Members can filter the catalogue by category and requested dates. The default view shows active items alphabetically. Search matches item names without case sensitivity. The baseline does not persist personal filter presets between visits. There are no equipment ratings, comments, image uploads or recommendation algorithms. Staff can update descriptive text, but inventory identifiers remain stable so that older reservations continue to reference the same physical item.
REQ-001.heading: HD-CATALOGUE — Equipment information

REQ-001.text:
## HD-USABILITY — Accessibility and interaction

Core reservation and reporting actions must be usable with a keyboard. Inputs have visible labels, focus remains visible and status is not communicated by color alone. Validation errors identify the affected field and explain how to correct it. After a failed submission, entered values remain in the form unless retaining a sensitive value would be inappropriate. Dates use an unambiguous display format and identify the cooperative's timezone where confusion is possible.

The supported viewport range is from a narrow mobile browser to a desktop browser. Tables may use a compact layout on smaller screens but cannot hide the reservation reference or status. No custom design system, animation framework or native mobile application is required. The baseline has no numeric response-time target, so phrases such as fast, instant or smooth require measurable clarification. Accessibility is part of the release criteria rather than optional visual polish.
REQ-001.heading: HD-USABILITY — Accessibility and interaction

## HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules

Members select one equipment item, a start date and an end date. Reservations use whole calendar days in the cooperative's configured local timezone. A reservation may begin no more than fourteen calendar days after the date of submission. This fourteen-day advance-booking limit applies equally to members, coordinators and administrators. Staff cannot silently bypass it through an alternative form. The maximum reservation duration is three consecutive calendar days, including the start date.

Reservations must not overlap for the same item. A successful reservation receives a stable reference and appears in the member's reservation list. The confirmation page shows the selected item and dates. A declined request does not create a provisional booking or reserve inventory. If the item becomes unavailable before submission, the member sees an actionable availability message. Retrying the same completed submission must not create another reservation.

Members may cancel their own reservation until its start date. Coordinators can cancel any reservation with a required reason. Cancellation releases the reserved interval and records who cancelled it. Recurring reservations, automatic renewal, waiting lists and subscriptions to newly available slots are not included in this baseline. A member who cancels a request is not automatically offered a different item. Recommendations and automatic substitutions require a separate decision about acceptable equipment equivalence.
REQ-002.heading: HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules

Invitations create an opportunity to activate an account, not a bypass around authentication.

Coordinators can inspect all reservations, confirm equipment handover and send account invitations. Administrators can assign roles, deactivate accounts and configure permitted operational settings. ## HD-PURPOSE — Purpose and release boundary

Harbor Desk lends cameras, projectors and portable audio kits to its members. Today coordinators reconcile reservations in a shared spreadsheet and answer availability questions by email. The portal should provide one reliable place to inspect availability, reserve an item and explain why a request cannot be completed. The first release serves one cooperative with a single equipment room and approximately two hundred active members. It does not support multiple organizations, payments, delivery routing or a public marketplace.

The cooperative wants a straightforward browser application. A person should understand whether a reservation succeeded without reading internal logs. Staff should be able to explain access decisions and reservation changes from the visible record. This release replaces reservation bookkeeping, not the cooperative's membership register. Membership verification remains an external administrative process. Names and examples in demonstrations must be invented. Demo records may be reset independently of any future operational deployment.

The application must distinguish availability from a confirmed reservation. Viewing a free slot does not hold it. Confirmation happens only after the server validates permissions, the reservation window and competing bookings. If two members request the same item and overlapping interval, only one request may succeed. The unsuccessful request must explain the conflict and allow the member to choose a different interval.

REQ-001.text:
## HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention

Role changes, reservation creation, cancellation and handover confirmation create audit events. Each event records an actor identifier, action, affected record identifier and timestamp. Audit records are append-only: ordinary users, coordinators and administrators cannot edit earlier events through the portal. Corrections are represented by a new event referencing the affected action. Passwords, invitation tokens and session tokens must never be recorded in audit data.

Audit events are retained for one hundred eighty days. A daily cleanup removes events older than that retention period. Administrators can view audit history for a particular affected record, but the baseline does not include a general actor filter or a free-text search across all events. Retaining audit data for a longer period changes the approved retention policy and requires explicit approval. Exporting report rows must not accidentally include audit payloads or account credentials.

The retention rule concerns audit events rather than active reservations. Removing an old audit event does not delete a current booking. Before changing retention, stakeholders must identify both the purpose of longer storage and the records it covers. A vague request to keep everything must not be interpreted as permission for indefinite retention.

## HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules

Every portal page containing equipment availability, reservations or reports requires a signed-in account. Anonymous visitors may see only a sign-in page and a generic description of the cooperative. Public sharing links and anonymous reservation views are excluded from the baseline. A copied reservation URL does not grant access; the server must apply the same authorization checks as ordinary navigation. Invitations create an opportunity to activate an account, not a bypass around authentication.

There are three roles: member, coordinator and administrator. Members can read the equipment catalogue and manage their own reservations. Coordinators can inspect all reservations, confirm equipment handover and send account invitations. Administrators can assign roles, deactivate accounts and configure permitted operational settings. Reports are visible to coordinators and administrators, but export is governed separately by HD-EXPORT. A coordinator may not promote themselves or another person to administrator.

Deactivating an account prevents subsequent sign-ins and new reservations. Existing reservation and audit records remain available to authorized staff. Deactivation must not erase the history that explains an equipment handover. This specification does not define guest, manager or external-collaborator roles. REQ-006.heading: HD-EXPORT — Report export permissions and format

## HD-EXPORT — Report export permissions and format

Only administrators may export reservation reports. Coordinators may view reports but may not download them. The server must enforce this restriction even when a coordinator sends an export request directly. Hiding the export button alone is insufficient. Members have no report export permission. Introducing another role with export permission is a change to the approved access policy, not a clarification of the existing behavior.

The initial export format is CSV encoded as UTF-8. Exported rows follow the active report filters and contain the same approved columns as the report. CSV values that could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas must be rendered safely. The filename includes the export date and does not contain a member's name. PDF, spreadsheet workbooks, scheduled delivery and a new monthly summary column are outside the baseline. Large reports may take time to prepare, but no asynchronous export queue is specified for the first release.

## HD-PURPOSE — Purpose and release boundary

Harbor Desk lends cameras, projectors and portable audio kits to its members. Today coordinators reconcile reservations in a shared spreadsheet and answer availability questions by email. REQ-006.heading: HD-INVITES — Invitation workflow
REQ-006.text:
## HD-INVITES — Invitation workflow

## HD-USABILITY — Accessibility and interaction

Core reservation and reporting actions must be usable with a keyboard. Inputs have visible labels, focus remains visible and status is not communicated by color alone. Validation errors identify the affected field and explain how to correct it. After a failed submission, entered values remain in the form unless retaining a sensitive value would be inappropriate. Dates use an unambiguous display format and identify the cooperative's timezone where confusion is possible.

The supported viewport range is from a narrow mobile browser to a desktop browser. Tables may use a compact layout on smaller screens but cannot hide the reservation reference or status. REQ-001.heading: HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules
REQ-001.text:
## HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules

Members select one equipment item, a start date and an end date. Reservations use whole calendar days in the cooperative's configured local timezone. A reservation may begin no more than fourteen calendar days after the date of submission. This fourteen-day advance-booking limit applies equally to members, coordinators and administrators. Staff cannot silently bypass it through an alternative form. The maximum reservation duration is three consecutive calendar days, including the start date.

Reservations must not overlap for the same item. A successful reservation receives a stable reference and appears in the member's reservation list. The confirmation page shows the selected item and dates. A declined request does not create a provisional booking or reserve inventory. If the item becomes unavailable before submission, the member sees an actionable availability message. Retrying the same completed submission must not create another reservation.

Members may cancel their own reservation until its start date. Coordinators can cancel any reservation with a required reason. Cancellation releases the reserved interval and records who cancelled it. Recurring reservations, automatic renewal, waiting lists and subscriptions to newly available slots are not included in this baseline. A member who cancels a request is not automatically offered a different item. Recommendations and automatic substitutions require a separate decision about acceptable equipment equivalence.

REQ-001.text:

An anonymous browser cannot view a copied private reservation link.

REQ-001.heading: HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention
REQ-001.text:
## HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention

Role changes, reservation creation, cancellation and handover confirmation create audit events. Each event records an actor identifier, action, affected record identifier and timestamp. Audit records are append-only: ordinary users, coordinators and administrators cannot edit earlier events through the portal. Corrections are represented by a new event referencing the affected action. Passwords, invitation tokens and session tokens must never be recorded in audit data.

REQ-003.heading: HD-INVITES — Invitation workflow
REQ-003.text:
## HD-INVITES — Invitation workflow

Coordinators and administrators may invite a prospective member by email. An invitation is single-use, expires after seventy-two hours and is tied to the addressed email account. The acceptance page explains whether an invitation is valid, expired or already used. Accepting an expired invitation does not create an account. Staff may issue a replacement invitation, which produces a new token and does not revive an expired token.

The invitation record contains the sender, addressed email, creation time, expiry time and acceptance time when applicable. The portal displays pending and accepted invitations separately. This release does not specify manual revocation of an unexpired invitation, reminder messages for pending invitations or bulk invitation uploads. Those are potential future features rather than implied behavior. An invitation token must not appear in operational logs or exports.

REQ-003.heading: HD-NOTIFY — Notifications
REQ-003.text:

REQ-003.heading: HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules
REQ-003.text:
## HD-BOOKING — Reservation rules

Members select one equipment item, a start date and an end date. Reservations use whole calendar days in the cooperative's configured local timezone. A reservation may begin no more than fourteen calendar days after the date of submission. This fourteen-day advance-booking limit applies equally to members, coordinators and administrators. Staff cannot silently bypass it through an alternative form. The maximum reservation duration is three consecutive calendar days, including the start date.

Reservations must not overlap for the same item. A successful reservation receives a stable reference and appears in the member's reservation list. The confirmation page shows the selected item and dates. A declined request does not create a provisional booking or reserve inventory. If the item becomes unavailable before submission, the member sees an actionable availability message. Retrying the same completed submission must not create another reservation.

Members may cancel their own reservation until its start date. Coordinators can cancel any reservation with a required reason. Cancellation releases the reserved interval and records who cancelled it. Recurring reservations, automatic renewal, waiting lists and subscriptions to newly available slots are not included in this baseline. A member who cancels a request is not automatically offered a different item. Recommendations and automatic substitutions require a separate decision about acceptable equipment equivalence.

REQ-006.heading: HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention
REQ-006.text:
## HD-AUDIT — Audit history and retention

Role changes, reservation creation, cancellation and handover confirmation create audit events. Each event records an actor identifier, action, affected record identifier and timestamp. Corrections are represented by a new event referencing the affected action. Passwords, invitation tokens and session tokens must never be recorded in audit data.

Audit events are retained for one hundred eighty days. A daily cleanup removes events older than that retention period. Administrators can view audit history for a particular affected record, but the baseline does not include a general actor filter or a free-text search across all events. Retaining audit data for a longer period changes the approved retention policy and requires explicit approval. Exporting report rows must not accidentally include audit payloads or account credentials.

The retention rule concerns audit events rather than active reservations. Removing an old audit event does not delete a current booking. Before changing retention, stakeholders must identify both the purpose of longer storage and the records it covers. A vague request to keep everything must not be interpreted as permission for indefinite retention.
